articles.content:
A number of people have been complaining that the new Siri demos during the keynote videos were a little on the slow side. There were notable lags of several seconds between Siri requests and the task being carried out.

But while the ideal we’re aiming for is for AI tasks to be carried out as quickly as possible, what we saw is kind of good news …

Apple was roundly criticised back in 2024 for using concept videos of features it was unable to demo.

What Apple showed regarding the upcoming “personalized Siri” at WWDC was not a demo. It was a concept video. Concept videos are bullshit, and a sign of a company in disarray, if not crisis.

That criticism was deserved, and Apple admitted that things were going to take longer than expected, deleted the offending video, and settled a $250M false advertising lawsuit.

The company seems to have learned its lesson. While the keynote wasn’t live, it does appear that all of the video demonstrations were conducted in real time, as TechCrunch noted.

Many of the Apple Intelligence demoes featured someone standing, phone in hand, pressing buttons or using voice commands in real time, while another camera showed off the phone’s response. These weren’t live onstage, anything-could-go wrong demos; they were pre-taped. But they looked far more like proof of working features than what Apple showed at WWDC 2024.

Indeed, John Gruber observed that there weren’t even any cuts between individual demos.

The demos were all shot in single takes, with no editing. In fact, I think most of them were single takes of multiple demos back-to-back.

What Apple showed off, then, appears to be a genuine reflection of how the new AI features work today. Joz actually says that because the demos were filmed a little ahead of WWDC, they were carried out with an older version of Siri AI, and it’s faster now:

We actually filmed these a bit in advance, that was Siri AI where it was at that point. You ask those same questions to it now, it’ll be faster, and at launch it will be faster still.

articles.title: How to keep your Mac awake, even when your MacBook lid is closed
articles.subtitle: macOS is designed to put your Mac to sleep when it is not being used. That is usually exactly what you want. Sleep saves power, protects battery life, and keeps a MacBook from running when it is closed and stuffed in a bag.
articles.author: 9to5Mac Apps
articles.content:
macOS is designed to put your Mac to sleep when it is not being used. That is usually exactly what you want. Sleep saves power, protects battery life, and keeps a MacBook from running when it is closed and stuffed in a bag.

Sometimes tasks like downloads, backups, remote sessions, and AI coding need a temporary exception. Fortunately, there are some great Mac apps for giving you this control.

Limited solutions that are included with macOS

Apple gives you some control in System Settings.

On macOS, you can go to System Settings > Lock Screen to change when the display turns off, and on Mac laptops you can use System Settings > Battery > Options to prevent automatic sleeping on the power adapter when the display is off.

Apple also supports using a Mac laptop with the lid closed when it is connected to power and paired with an external display, keyboard, and mouse or trackpad.

I generally prefer not to make those settings permanent. Most of the time, I want my Mac to sleep normally. What I want instead is a quick, intentional override that I can turn on for a specific job and turn off when I am done.

For that, there are three Mac utilities worth knowing.

KeepingYouAwake is the simple one-click toggle

KeepingYouAwake is the utility that has lived in my Mac menu bar the longest.

It is free, lightweight, and built around the same basic idea that made Caffeine popular years ago: click a menu bar icon, and your Mac stays awake. Click it again, and your Mac returns to its normal sleep behavior.

I started using KeepingYouAwake years ago when Macs moved to Retina displays. Caffeine, the classic coffee-cup utility, did not make that transition to high-resolution design.

KeepingYouAwake became the simple replacement. It honors the spirit of Caffeine with no dashboard or complex automation. It’s just a reliable on/off switch for the Mac’s default sleep behavior.

You can activate it indefinitely or for preset durations, and it can automatically disable itself when your MacBook battery drops below a set level. It supports Retina displays and Dark Mode, and under the hood it uses Apple’s built-in caffeinate command-line utility.

The important limitation: KeepingYouAwake is not the closed-lid solution. Its own documentation is clear that, because of macOS limitations and thermal considerations, it only prevents sleep on desktop Macs and portable Macs with the lid open.

That makes KeepingYouAwake ideal for the simple stuff: reading, presentations, screen recordings, long downloads, or any time you are still using the Mac and just do not want the screen or system to nod off. It is the utility I use as my everyday “do not sleep yet” toggle.

Amphetamine is the gold standard for closed-lid sessions

When I actually want to close my MacBook and keep a task running, Amphetamine is the app I open.

Yahoo Finance was one of those to attribute the slide to the WWDC announcements.

Apple Inc shares were down 4% on Tuesday afternoon after the company’s annual developer conference left some investors questioning the pace of its artificial intelligence rollout, even as analysts broadly viewed the event as a step forward […] Despite the reported improvements, analysts flagged meaningful limitations.

Siri AI will launch in beta later this year for supported devices set to English and will not be available initially in the European Union on iOS or iPadOS. articles.title: Xbox CEO Lays Out Post-Layoff Priorities For Ambitious Growth After A Terrible Year
articles.subtitle: A new Asha Sharma memo has hit Xbox. In it, the CEO shed light on her core priorities and goals to get Microsoft’s gaming division back to strong growth and profits after another 1,600 of its employees were laid off at the beginning of the month.
articles.author: Kotaku
articles.content:
A new Asha Sharma memo has hit Xbox. In it, the CEO shed light on her core priorities and goals to get Microsoft’s gaming division back to strong growth and profits after another 1,600 of its employees were laid off at the beginning of the month. Among other things, the plan calls for Xbox to be halfway to a stated goal of 1 billion users per day. It’s currently at 100 million.

Insight into Sharma’s plan comes from The Verge, which shared excerpts from the latest memo to be sent to Xbox staff on July 30. In its earnings report this week, Microsoft reported double-digit declines in revenue on both the hardware and games and services sides, with total revenue for the year declining by $1.7 billion. Xbox’s new CEO laid out four main priorities to pull the platform out of that tailspin in the next fiscal year:

CORE: Strengthen our platform, led by console CONTENT: Grow great games into global franchises CREATION: Make Minecraft the world’s creator platform CONNECTION: Extend the worlds that fans love

CORE: Strengthen our platform, led by console

CONTENT: Grow great games into global franchises

CREATION: Make Minecraft the world’s creator platform

CONNECTION: Extend the worlds that fans love

While each priority begins with the letter C, the actions entailed in following through on them are less obvious. Heading into 2028 and 2029, the plan is to “move into businesses producing meaningful player value and revenue acceleration.” By 2030, the goal is to be “halfway to our long-term daily-player goal with sustained double-digit growth in players and engagement and industry leading margins.”

In her now infamous “reset” memo announcing cuts to 3,600 Xbox employees over the next 12 months, including closing or spinning off several studios, Sharma said she wanted Xbox to be one of the few companies that “entertains” more than a billion people each day. Today’s memo stated that Xbox is currently at 100 million. Getting halfway to a billion within four years would seem to require unprecedented growth of nearly 50 percent annually.

Sharma went on to call Xbox “one of the largest stadiums in the world,” a metaphor reminiscent of Google’s failed Stadia play, and said that while the Xbox console remains a “flagship experience,” Xbox will also be searching for new players through PC, cloud, and other platforms.

Long-term plans include monetizing big franchises like Fallout “across film, television, consumer products, sponsorship, live experiences, and form new partnerships globally, including China,” as well plowing even more investment to Candy Crush and Minecraft.

At one point, the CEO reportedly mentioned being more focused on not just the company’s biggest franchises but its “biggest new ideas.” It looks like we’ll have to wait a little longer to find out what those might be.

articles.title: When Find My doesn’t help with separation anxiety
articles.subtitle: I dispense what might be called valuable insight to my friends, as well as in this public forum. My friends know the danger: they might become the topic of a column, which is true for my buddy Jeff, who left a bag containing his passport behind at a hotel.…
articles.author: Six Colors
articles.content:
I dispense what might be called valuable insight to my friends, as well as in this public forum. My friends know the danger: they might become the topic of a column, which is true for my buddy Jeff, who left a bag containing his passport behind at a hotel. Fortunately, he had an AirTag in his bag. That was, however, just the beginning of the journey. (Jeff gave me permission to share his story.) 1

To avoid suspense, I’ll tell you that Jeff doesn’t have his bag back, but will soon.

Grate news

Jeff was out of town on business for a few days—he’s one of those nearly extinct creatures called a “ full-time technology reporter “—and was carrying his passport to Texas not because it’s another country (it hasn’t seceded yet), but because he lacks a Real ID-upgraded driver’s license.

He had a small bag with a few items, including the passport and an AirTag, that he didn’t need to carry, so he used the hotel safe. There have been many articles written about how unsafe hotel safes are, but it feels as if you’re in a decent hotel, it’s still another bar for someone to get through to steal your stuff.

Leaving in a bit of a rush, Jeff didn’t retrieve the bag from the safe. When he realized it wasn’t with him, thousands of miles later, he was peeved. Shouldn’t the “left behind” feature in Find My have alerted him? Find My showed the bag’s location, however. For some reason, it appeared as if it were in the hotel parking lot. I catastrophized with him, assuming it was stolen. He called the hotel, which said it wasn’t in lost and found.

A staff member went out, looked in the parking lot, and said the rough location was a grate—perhaps the bag had been stolen and someone had found the AirTag and dropped it through the slats? Which would imply that a hotel employee or a thief had managed to get into Jeff’s room after he left, open the safe, leave the hotel, and rummage through the bag in the parking lot before absconding.

That wasn’t the case (or valise). The hotel called back the next day. The previous staffer didn’t know, for some reason, that valuable left-behind items were tagged and placed in a safe in the basement, presumably below or near the parking lot. His bag, containing his passport and other items, would be sent back to him.

Jeff’s experience reveals several aspects of the Find My tracking system that you can take advantage of in advance or use if you’ve lost something or left it behind.

Don’t leave me!

Every device and item you have can be set to alert you when you “leave it behind.” I believe this setting is enabled by default, though Apple’s documentation isn’t clear on this point. All of my devices and items have it enabled, and Jeff found it was turned on for all his gear. Here’s how to check:

In a native Find My app, select the device (like a Mac) or an item (an AirTag or other Find My network item) in the list of such things.

On an iPhone, iPad, or Apple Watch, the action sheet appears. On a Mac, click the info (i) icon next to the item’s name on the map. In the upcoming version 27 operating system releases on all platforms, tap or click the More (…) button that appears when you select the device from the list.

Tap or click Notify When Left Behind, which should already show On. (In the 27 releases, tap or click When Left Behind.)

If disabled, turn it on.

Here’s a crucial detail: examine the “Notify me, except at” list. You can manually add to this set of locations (tap or click New Location). However, it primarily grows when you’re notified by an item or device being left behind, and then you tap or click in the notification to ignore it at that location. You are presented with the option to just exclude that item or device from that location or all of your equipment.

It’s very easy to approve that exclude-all button. (Jeff did not; his list didn’t include the hotel.) This can be convenient when you’re at a hotel, a friend’s house, or another location for a few days or frequently, and sometimes leave Find My-tracked stuff there. But once you ignore the location, you won’t get notified in the future. You can modify the list by hand, too.

Jeff may instead have been tripped up by the safe acting as a Faraday cage—a metal mesh or box that shields electromagnetic signals from passing through. The AirTag and other Find My items use Bluetooth to broadcast a rotating identifier at regular intervals. 2 If the safe blocked that signal, Jeff’s iPhone lost contact with the AirTag the moment the bag went in—a few days before he left.

articles.title: The better way to use Gemini on the Mac
articles.subtitle: Back in April, Google joined OpenAI and Anthropic in offering a dedicated Mac app for its AI chatbot software. Two months later, it’s clear that Gemini for Mac isn’t as good as it could be.
articles.author: 9to5Mac Apps
articles.content:
Back in April, Google joined OpenAI and Anthropic in offering a dedicated Mac app for its AI chatbot software. Two months later, it’s clear that Gemini for Mac isn’t as good as it could be.

Gemini for Mac isn’t a very good macOS app

Because I’m interested in AI technology and its progression over time, I’ve used Gemini on my Mac regularly since before the Mac app was rumored.

I’m also a Safari user. For that reason, my solution to using Gemini on the Mac has been Safari’s “Add to Dock” feature.

When Gemini first arrived on the Mac as a dedicated app, I still preferred my Safari “Add to Dock” instance. I just like that Command + N opens a new chat window, and I can have many open chat windows.

This way of multitasking is better for me than switching between conversation threads. I’m more likely to forget about a task in a chat thread if it’s not an open window on my Mac.

Missing features and app icon jail

I also have at least one chat thread that doesn’t actually work on Gemini’s Mac app. It works fine in the Safari “Add to Dock” version, though, since that’s just the website presented as an app.

Instead of letting me continue the chat, Gemini’s Mac app replaces the text entry box with a button to open the website. I’d rather just use my Safari web app version where it works fine.

The use of the word “yet” in the message is doing a lot of work at this point.

Another complaint is the icon. Gemini’s Mac app is in icon jail.

Icon jail is a dumb Apple behavior for app icons on macOS Tahoe that aren’t drawn in the exact shape and size that Apple forces.

While that’s an Apple-forced problem for Mac apps that predate Apple’s dumb rule, the Gemini Mac app arrived months after macOS Tahoe was released.

Then there’s the thing that prompted me to mention how I’m using Gemini on my Mac in the first place.

This week on Daring Fireball, John Gruber wrote about why he uninstalled the Gemini Mac app:

The thing that really turns me off about the Gemini Mac app is Google’s gall. The Gemini app installs a background helper named “GeminiAppLauncher” in your login items. It also installs “GoogleUpdater” as a process with the privilege to launch in the background whenever it wants. Gemini never asks for permission to install either of these, and, most arrogantly, if you, as an informed user, remove either of them, the Gemini app silently adds them back. There is no setting in Gemini to disable this.

This made me realize that I’ve literally kept the Gemini Mac app around just to check for app updates. While there are occasional updates, they haven’t fixed my two issues with the software yet.

articles.title: Apple’s AI announcements: One big question, and 11 key features
articles.subtitle: Almost two years after Apple first showed off a video promoting the new Siri and lots of exciting new Apple Intelligence features, that future has finally arrived – at least in first beta form. The company had a lot of ground to make up.
articles.author: 9to5Mac Apple Intelligence
articles.content:
Almost two years after Apple first showed off a video promoting the new Siri and lots of exciting new Apple Intelligence features, that future has finally arrived – at least in first beta form.

The company had a lot of ground to make up. Obviously, the test will be how well the new features work in real life usage, but let’s start with what seemed to me to be the most important things the company announced …

The big iPhone support question

For me, one of the biggest questions to arise from the keynote was exactly what features will require the iPhone 17 Pro and up?

Apple had three things to say about iPhone support. The first says that any phone capable of running iOS 26 can be upgraded to iOS 27. That means all the way back to the iPhone 11.

The second is that the new AI features only extend back to the iPhone 15 Pro:

Apple Intelligence and Siri AI in iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, watchOS 27, and visionOS 27 are available on iPhone 16 models or later, iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max.

The third says that some features are limited to just the latest and greatest models.

Apple’s most powerful on-device model and the features it enables, like expressive voices and more advanced dictation, are available on iPhone Air, iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max.

The word ‘like’ is doing a lot of heavy lifting there: it means we don’t yet know what other features will fall into this category. Additionally, it’s not yet 100% clear whether phones that can’t perform these actions on-device will still get access to the same features, just relying on cloud connectivity.

This latter question is especially important when it comes to advanced dictation. However smart the new Siri may be, it first needs to understand what we are saying. The existing Siri speech-to-text capabilities fall way short of what is available from third-parties.

The overall model seems well-considered

Apple’s general approach here is to make Siri’s new capabilities transparently available system-wide. In other words, we can ask our iPhone to do something and the new Siri will step in to perform the task.

However, there are times when it’s useful to revisit an earlier chatbot session, and Apple allows us to do this through the Siri app. That seems to me the best of both worlds. We don’t need to open Siri to do anything requiring the new Apple Intelligence features, but we can access past sessions when required.

Agentic AI is key

The ability to ask our iPhone to carry out a task and have it be able to access not only the personal information we have stored on our phone, but also interact with apps, is absolutely key to truly useful AI.

Again, we will need to see how well this really works, but Apple does seem to be ticking all of the boxes in terms of the capabilities I was looking for.

Privacy is core

articles.title: 10 biggest D&D announcements from Gen Con 2026
articles.subtitle: Wizards of the Coast has firmly established Gen Con as a major annual event for Dungeons & Dragons announcements Related Dungeons & Dragons has officially cemented Gen Con as the premiere event during which Wizards of the Coast will announce each upcoming...
articles.author: Polygon
articles.content:
Wizards of the Coast has firmly established Gen Con as a major annual event for Dungeons & Dragons announcements

Related

Dungeons & Dragons has officially cemented Gen Con as the premiere event during which Wizards of the Coast will announce each upcoming year’s slate of TTRPG content. During Thursday night’s D&D Vision Keynote 2027 panel hosted by Baldur’s Gate 3 ’s Theo Solomon, D&D designers and leadership talked about new releases for the game, including updates on new books, digital tools, video games, and collaborations for the next year and more.

Some announcements fill gaps in D&D’s previously announced lineup, including a renewed commitment to publishing full-length adventures. Others revive beloved campaign settings that have gone unsupported for years. The biggest reveal establishes an entire program dedicated to prominent crossovers, starting with a fittingly epic tabletop adaptation of a popular fantasy video game.

Here are the nine biggest D&D announcements from Gen Con 2026.

D&D Icons reunites the game’s most influential creators

Wizards of the Coast is bringing some of D&D’s foundational creators back into the fold through a new initiative called D&D Icons.

“The goal is to bring together legendary creators with the current design team to help shape future content,” franchise creative director Kara Kenna said during a presentation ahead of Gen Con, describing it as “a new initiative that brings together some of the most iconic and influential creators in D&D's history to work on new stories from their unique voice.”

Joe Manganiello will serve as chief creative officer of the initiative, which begins with three pillars of D&D history. Dragonlance creators Margaret Weis and Tracy Hickman are also involved, as is R.A. Salvatore, author of the Legend of Drizzt novels.

The program’s first collaborator is Luke Gygax, who will contribute to upcoming Greyhawk material, which includes content drawn from unpublished notes left by his father, D&D co-creator Gary Gygax. “This is just the beginning of this exciting program,” Kenna said. “Who knows who we might bring to the table?”

Third-party studios will make official D&D adventures

D&D has accumulated dozens of campaign settings over its five-decade history, but maintaining all of them has proven impossible for Wizards’ internal team, which will often focus on settings like the Forgotten Realms while others, ironically, remain mostly forgotten. Wizards will enlist prominent third-party publishers to make official D&D books.

“Players shouldn’t have to wait decades before we go back to an Eberron or a Ravenloft or a Dark Sun,” executive producer Greg Bilsland said. “We should be making it easier for everybody to run adventures.”

The first of these partnerships will produce an official Ravenloft book from Ghostfire Gaming in 2027 that incorporates the Domains of Dread recently featured in Ravenloft: The Horrors Within. An Eberron adventure featuring the Lord of Blades will follow in 2028 from Visionary Productions, while Kobold Press will develop new Forgotten Realms material.

These won’t be lightly affiliated supplements published through the Dungeon Masters Guild, which has been the case for quite some time with similar products. They will be official physical and digital D&D releases sold through Wizards of the Coast’s normal distribution channels.

“A big piece of what we’re trying to do here is provide annual support for every one of our settings,” Bilsland said. The exact format may vary between a singular campaign and an adventure anthology, but Wizards’ goal is to provide one major adventure for each supported setting every year in some capacity.

D&D Beyond is getting a major overhaul

Finding a reliable D&D group remains one of the biggest obstacles to actually playing the game. Wizards is trying to address that problem with a new looking-for-group hub at dndbeyond.com/lfg.

articles.title: Apple Launches Apple Upgrade: Here’s How the New iPhone, Apple Watch, Mac, and iPad Lease Program Works
articles.subtitle: Apple has introduced a new program aimed at making an upgrade to the company’s latest products a bit more manageable for price-conscious customers. The company is calling the program Apple Upgrade and it replaces the previous iPhone Upgrade Program.
articles.author: OWC Rocket Yard
articles.content:
Apple has introduced a new program aimed at making an upgrade to the company’s latest products a bit more manageable for price-conscious customers. The company is calling the program Apple Upgrade and it replaces the previous iPhone Upgrade Program.

And while Apple Upgrade is designed to deliver new Apple products at reasonable monthly payments, it works a bit differently than the previous upgrade program or Apple’s current Apple Card Monthly Installments. That’s because it’s a lease program built in partnership with Klarna. Apple Upgrade is live in the Apple Store now, so let’s talk about how it works so you’ll know if the new program makes sense for you.

How Apple Upgrade Works

Because Apple Upgrade is a lease program, it works similarly to a car lease in that you are not financing a purchase. Instead, because Apple is running the program through Klarna, Klarna is the owner of any device you lease through the program and you pay a set monthly payment to lease the device from them.

Apple is offering lease terms of 12 or 24 months for iPhone and Apple Watch. For Mac and iPad leases, the program offers 24- or 36-month terms. You’ll have to enroll in the program to use it which requires being approved through a soft credit check that Apple says won’t affect your credit score.

Once approved, you’ll pick your device and pay a monthly payment for that device until the end of your lease. Apple says leasing prices start as low as $17.99 per month for iPhone, $11.99 for Apple Watch, $24.99 for Mac, and $11.99 for iPad. At the end of your lease you have a decision to make: pay to purchase the device or send it back to Apple.

And here’s a very important detail for those worried about whether the Apple Upgrade program is a “trap” or is based in predatory lending practices: leases through the program are not subject to interest. There is a discussion to be had about who the program makes the most sense for and whether you’re taking full advantage of the intrinsic value of an Apple device, and we get into that below.

But you can rest assured that none of your payments will be going to interest and that’s the big difference between this lease and a typical car lease.

So, if there’s no interest, your next question might be “How are the monthly payments Apple is offering through Apple Upgrade lower than what a no-interest financing plan would offer for the same device?” The answer is that because this is a lease and not a financed purchase, the monthly payments are calculated differently.

Depending on the lease term you agree to, the program starts by essentially guessing what the value of your device will be at the end of your lease in order to calculate the residual value of your device. Once they have an estimated residual value, they subtract that residual from the total purchase price and then divide that figure by however many months your lease term spans. So the lease payments are lower than financing because you’re dividing a lower figure than the total purchase price.

Let’s take a look at the Apple Upgrade pricing for an iPhone 17 Pro Max with 256GB of storage to see how this works.

An Example Lease Through Apple Upgrade

iPhone 17 Pro Max 256GB: $1,199 purchase price $1,199 – $359.24 (estimated residual value after 24 months) = $839.76 (This is the fiigure the program divides by the total number of payments you’ll make over the lease term.) $839.76 / 24 = $34.99 per month.

In this example, you would lease the iPhone 17 Pro Max by making payments of $34.99 per month for 24 months. Once your lease is up, you’ll be able to pay an estimated $359.24 to purchase the phone and cover its residual value. Or you can ship the device back to Apple and buy or lease a new iPhone.

Other Things to be Aware Of

Apple does allow you to combine a trade-in with Apple Upgrade to lower your monthly payment even further. Plus, if you use your Apple Card to pay your lease, you do get 3% cash back on those payments.

Another crucial detail is that the payment program is handled through the Klarna app rather than the Apple Store app.

And while you can add AppleCare+ or AppleCare One to a device leased through Apple Upgrade, AppleCare is not included with your lease.

articles.title: Lil Finder Guy pet was the gateway to building my own Mac apps with Codex
articles.subtitle: At the start of May, OpenAI released a playful feature inside its Codex desktop app for creating a virtual pet. This silly little addition solved my biggest challenge with Codex: what should I do with it?
articles.author: 9to5Mac Apps
articles.content:
At the start of May, OpenAI released a playful feature inside its Codex desktop app for creating a virtual pet.

This silly little addition solved my biggest challenge with Codex: what should I do with it? My first real task with Codex was putting together a virtual Lil Finder Guy for fun.

A month later, I’m using two Mac apps that Codex built at my direction. Toying around with Codex Pets was the gateway for me to better understand its capabilities.

OpenAI tools for making apps have improved a lot since last summer

Both Mac apps are just for my use and not intended for distribution, but that’s just a choice and not a Codex limitation. They’re genuinely usable and useful software applications that serve my needs.

One tool is called Flow, and it just helps me track activity and changes around the App Store. Another offers a better experience with using a social network on the Mac without certain constraints of Chrome, like minimum window width.

The experience taught me just how much these tools have changed since this time last year as well.

For example, I wanted to make my own Launchpad replacement when macOS Tahoe removed the feature from the Mac last June. (Launchpad wasn’t for everyone, but it was part of my muscle memory since OS X Lion. I’ve since moved on from missing it.)

Using ChatGPT to walk me through Xcode while copying and pasting blocks of code and screenshots of errors was a process void of much joy. Even as a proof-of-concept, I couldn’t get the app that I was making to resemble the behavior that I had in mind. Nuking the project felt good.

With Codex, I had a functioning app that solved my specific need in almost no time (and literally no Xcode). I was able to go from idea to minimum viable software almost immediately. The rest of my first month with Codex and making the app was spent adding features beyond my original need and getting more specific about how things should look and behave.

There are more tools that I want to make for myself next, and having Codex’s capabilities on the Mac has been a real boost.

(Next, I’ll be watching Apple’s WWDC announcements with a new eye for what additional capabilities become available. I’m also cautious about any changes that may break my newfound system for turning ideas into functioning tools.)

Computer Use in Codex is a major unlock

Part of what makes Codex good at this compared to my experience using ChatGPT a year ago is that the model and app are made for coding and generally just doing things for you.

ChatGPT will absorb most or all of this functionality as a feature within the main app, but the extent of this remains to be seen. For now, there’s one thing in particular about Codex that made all the difference in the world: Computer Use.

Codex is far from the only coding agent available on the Mac, and it’s not the only version with a computer use feature either. But Codex’s Computer Use feature is phenomenal. On the Mac, it works in the background without taking over your machine. For me, this has meant I’ve been able to use my Mac, uninterrupted, while this coding agent expertly follows my direction.

Codex’s Computer Use essentially unlocks the complete opposite experience from what ChatGPT provided in this department last summer. Instead of it providing me with guidance and not much perspective, I’ve been able to guide it and vastly expand my own perspective.

You don’t have to spend a lot to get Codex experience
